Vivian Dandridge was found at the victim’s rooms in the brownstone. The cigarette he had going burned itself out on the sill where it fell. The bells at St. Malachy’s came at 9:30 PM, and the bells fix it: the sexton rings them off the sacristy clock and it keeps good time. That puts the killing in that half hour and no later.
The coroner puts death between 8:30 PM and 10:00 PM — two hours of nothing useful. One bullet below the sternum. Powder burns on the shirt front: fired close.
A nickel-plated revolver is gone from the speakeasy under the hat shop. The drawer it was kept in is open and the oiled cloth is still in it.

candidates.text: Thomas Hanrahan claims to have been at the speakeasy under the hat shop at 9:00 PM but cannot say that the challenger went down in the fourth and the crowd booed it, which everybody there can.
Found at the victim’s rooms in the brownstone: A draft codicil in Vivian Dandridge’s hand striking Ezekiel Hargrove out of the will, dated last Tuesday and unsigned.
Verity Coffin says Vivian Dandridge told Ezekiel Hargrove the lawyer was coming Thursday and that the arrangement would be changed.
Found at the victim’s rooms in the brownstone: A subpoena naming Vivian Dandridge before the grand jury, with Thomas Hanrahan’s name written in the margin.
Concetta Petrosino says Vivian Dandridge said to Thomas Hanrahan that a man who testifies sleeps better.
Found at the victim’s rooms in the brownstone: A clipping about the failure of Concetta Petrosino’s business, with Vivian Dandridge’s name underlined twice in pencil.
Ezekiel Hargrove says Concetta Petrosino said Vivian Dandridge had taken everything and would be made to feel it.
Found at the victim’s rooms in the brownstone: A promissory note for $4,000 signed by Albrecht Lindemann, endorsed to Vivian Dandridge, three months past due.
Concetta Petrosino says Vivian Dandridge told Albrecht Lindemann that Friday was the end of it, one way or the other.
